The money a month has to spare after spending, debt payments, saving, investing and pots are taken off. It uses the kind of month picked under Check against. A pot is money kept for one cost, on a set date.
Every check starts here. A purchase lowers it by its monthly cost. Saving and investing are the only things a check can pause to make up a gap.

Paid from this month’s spare: it fits in what the month has after saving and investing. Paid from savings: cash stays above your minimum. Too big to pay at once: paying in one go would take cash below your minimum.

How many months of your costs the cash you would still hold could pay for, after this purchase and the bills due in the next 90 days.
The least cash to keep, on the day or before the next payday. If left empty, the app uses 3 months of your costs when income is steady, 4.5 when it varies and 6 when it varies a lot.

A pot is money kept for one cost, with a target amount and a date. Each month, what is still needed is divided by the months to go (rounded up) and taken off your spare money. Money already in a pot is kept out of what a check can use.
Your other open checks are counted as if you bought them too. Two purchases can each fit alone but not together; this shows that.
